title: These Unemployment Numbers Are Going Up
text:
These Unemployment Numbers Are Going Up

Andrew Batson

Gavekal Dragonomics | 12 Aug 2026

There may be no Chinese economic statistic with a longer history of being utterly useless than the unemployment rate. For decades, China reported only a “registered” urban unemployment rate that was amazingly steady around 4%, failing to reflect massive shocks like the layoffs from state enterprises or the 2008 global financial crisis. That was probably because it covered only a restricted group with access to official unemployment benefits, whose numbers the authorities had strong incentives to control. After years of criticism, that indicator was replaced by a “surveyed” unemployment rate, with broader coverage and a definition closer to international standards. But aside from a brief spike during the pandemic, that rate has also been amazingly steady around 5%. Despite their technical differences, both headline unemployment rates have in practice delivered little information about changes in the job market.
